quizName: DMV Practice Test #14 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: To turn safely on a motorcycle, you should always:

options.text: Lean in the direction of the curve.
Turn by using only the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lean in the direction of the curve.
questions.explanation: Lean your body in the direction you are turning. Slow down before you enter the turn, not during it.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn your head, shoulders, and torso.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head.
questions.explanation: Turn only your head when looking through a turn. Keep your shoulders still and your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: You should increase your following distance:

options.text: If you can see through the vehicles in front of you to determine traffic conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: If the pavement is slippery.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance if your motorcycle takes longer to stop. This includes slippery pavement, heavy traffic, or when you cannot see past the vehicle ahead. Use at least a four-second following distance in these conditions.

questions.question: If wearing a jacket for protection while riding in hot weather, you should:

options.text: Take frequent breaks to cool off.
Remove the jacket to stay cool while in the sun.
Keep the jacket on to protect you from the heat.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the jacket on to protect you from the heat.
questions.explanation: Wear your jacket in any weather to protect yourself in a crash. Jackets also help prevent dehydration in hot weather. Many riding jackets are designed to keep you from overheating.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slippery when wet
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They alert drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the road will be slippery when wet.

questions.question: If you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle:

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
You should flash your headlight to tell the other vehicle to proceed.
You should continue through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or traffic lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: You must come to a complete stop.
You may go through the intersection carefully.
You must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red light. Stop completely and wait for a signal that allows you to turn in the direction you want to go.

questions.question: When riding at night, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Increase your following distance.
questions.explanation: At night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance to prevent crashes. Use the headlights of vehicles ahead to see farther. Stay flexible with your lane position at night.

questions.question: To swerve correctly, you should:

options.text: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Press the handgrip in the direction of the turn.
questions.explanation: To swerve away from danger, gently press the handgrip on the side where you want to go.

questions.question: Before you start riding, make sure the fuel valve is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Open.
questions.explanation: Always open the fuel valve before you ride. If it is closed, the engine may start using fuel left in the lines, but it will stall once that fuel runs out.

questions.question: To make a quick turn, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Lean your motorcycle quickly.
questions.explanation: To make a quick turn, lean your motorcycle in the direction you want to turn. The sharper the turn, the more you must lean.

questions.question: Service signs are:
questions.correctAnswerText: Blue with white letters.
questions.explanation: Blue signs with white letters show where services are located. These include rest areas, gas stations, food, and hospitals.

questions.question: Shifting gears while turning:

options.text: Should only be done if it can be done smoothly.
Is better than shifting before the turn.
Is the best way to control your speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should only be done if it can be done smoothly.
questions.explanation: Change gears before you start a turn. If you must shift while turning, do it smoothly. A sudden change in power can cause your rear wheel to skid.

questions.question: One of the best ways to help others see your motorcycle is:

options.text: Keep your high beam headlight on.
Paint your motorcycle a dark color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your high beam headlight on.
questions.explanation: The best way to help others see your motorcycle is to use your high beam headlight. Use it during the day and night whenever it is legal and safe.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle stopped on the side of the road with flashing lights. You should:

options.text: Stop on the roadway behind the emergency vehicle.
Stop and wait until the emergency vehicle starts moving again.
Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to a different lane away from the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: Move into a different lane to give the emergency vehicle extra space. Slow down and be ready to stop when you see an emergency scene.

questions.question: If a dog is chasing you, you should:

options.text: Stop your motorcycle until the dog loses interest.
Slow down as the dog approaches, then quickly speed up and away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down as the dog approaches, then quickly speed up and away.
questions.explanation: If a dog approaches your motorcycle, slow down and downshift. Quickly speed up and away as the dog gets close.

questions.question: To avoid confusing other drivers, you should:

options.text: Keep more distance between you and the vehicle ahead.
Turn off your turn signal after you finish turning or changing lanes.
Use your horn only in emergencies.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off your turn signal after you finish turning or changing lanes.
questions.explanation: Turn off your signal after you complete a turn or lane change. Leaving it on confuses other drivers.

questions.question: When riding in a group, less experienced riders should be:
questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the lead rider.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride near the front, just behind the leader. This way, experienced riders can watch them from behind.

questions.question: When following another vehicle, position yourself so the driver can see you in:
questions.correctAnswerText: The rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Follow in the center of your lane. The driver will most likely see you in their rearview mirror. Drivers check their rearview mirrors much more often than their side mirrors.

questions.question: When passing a truck on a two-lane road, return to your lane when:

options.text: You can see the entire front of the truck in your rearview mirror.
You feel you have enough space.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can see the entire front of the truck in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Only return to your original lane when you can see the entire front of the truck in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: Is eye protection required?

options.text: Yes, it is required for all riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yes, it is required for all riders.
questions.explanation: Georgia law requires all motorcycle riders to wear eye protection. A full face shield gives the best protection.

questions.question: How should you ride over grooved pavement in a work zone?

options.text: Look down to watch the road surface.
Keep your head and eyes up.
Move to the edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your head and eyes up.
questions.explanation: Keep your head and eyes up when riding through a work zone. Ride slowly over the grooved pavement.

questions.question: Where should you ride when passing parked cars?

options.text: On the left side of the lane.
On the right side of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the left side of the lane.
questions.explanation: The left side of the lane is safest when passing parked cars. This position helps you avoid open doors, people stepping out, and cars pulling out. Always be ready to adjust your position for changing conditions.

questions.question: Where is the front brake lever usually located?
questions.correctAnswerText: On the right handle grip.
questions.explanation: The front brake lever is usually on the right handle grip. Learn where all controls are before riding.

questions.question: Which lane position makes a motorcycle most visible to other drivers?
questions.correctAnswerText: The center
questions.explanation: The center position is usually best when following a car. It places you in the driver's rearview mirror. Be ready to change positions if traffic or conditions require it.
